Subject: EU launch — temporary SLA provisioning exception & credit escrow request

Hi Rishi,

We're targeting EU-West launch of Aurora Search on June 1. The first 6 weeks after launch will have unusually high burst traffic (indexing and bulk re-ranks) and some traffic patterns that will push us above the provisioned pools you recommended.

Quick ask: would Redwood consider a short-term SLA provisioning exception for the EU region for the first 60 days so we can rely on temporary burst capacity without immediate latency remediation penalties? In parallel, we'd like to set up a monthly "credit escrow" that caps any service credits triggered during that period (Aurora proposes a $20k cap per month) and applies those credits to remediation/engineering assistance once the initial ramp completes.

We understand why standard uptime % and credit mechanics exist — this is a risk-sharing ask to prevent surprise invoices while we stabilize. If helpful, I've attached our projected usage spike and a short note from our SRE on burst windows.

Can you propose concrete amendment language (uptime numbers, carve-out window definition, credit cap mechanics) that your legal/product teams would accept? We're ready to expedite procurement paperwork once terms are in place.

Thanks,
Elena Martinez
Head of Platform
Aurora Systems

Attachments: usage-projections-may-june.csv
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Elena Martinez <elena@aurorasys.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 14 May 2025 15:02:00 +0000
Subject: Re: EU launch — temporary SLA provisioning exception & credit escrow request

Hi Elena — thanks for the heads up and the projection file. Congrats on the upcoming launch.

High level proposal (we can iterate):
- Standard uptime commitment remains 99.9% for Redwood-hosted EU services when traffic is within provisioned capacity.
- Temporary burst carve-out: for the first 60 days after go-live, define a \"burst window\" equal to the sum of minutes where Aurora's 5-minute rolling QPS exceeds the provisioned pool by more than 40%. During the burst window, we will not apply latency remediation credits for P95 latency degradations related to known onboarding traffic patterns. (We will still apply credits for complete service availability loss.)
- Monthly credit escrow: cap total monthly service credits applied to Aurora's invoices at the lesser of $15,000 or 10% of the month's Redwood invoice. Credits exceeding the cap will be documented and held in escrow; funds will be applied toward post-launch remediation work (engineering time, priority support) within 90 days of the 60-day ramp period or refunded if remediation not performed.
- Measurement & region: metrics and measurements will be by region (eu-west) using Redwood's observability dashboard; Aurora will have read-only access.
- Term: 60-day carve-out starting at Aurora's declared go-live timestamp.

I've attached a short amendment draft for you to review (PDF). Laura and Kimberly are CC'd to weigh in on the legal and commercial guardrails. If this looks directionally acceptable, we can prepare a DocuSign-ready amendment and a simple PO reference.

Two quick clarifications for your team: 1) Do you need the carve-out to apply to both availability and latency, or only latency? 2) Is the proposed cap ($15k or 10%) in the right ballpark?

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
